# Current implementation record

**GitHub Pages preparation (2026-11-21):** added a main-branch/manual Actions
workflow that builds with Node 24 and Python 3.12, then deploys only `dist/`
through the official Pages actions. A build-time venv supports the existing
prebuild progress script without native scientific packages. Added
`public/CNAME` for openswing.vibefoil.com, `.nojekyll`, canonical/social URL
metadata, a web manifest and Daedalus-derived SVG/ICO/Apple/app icons. Source
downloads now include the static branding/domain assets and workflow. Icon
dimensions/ICO frames, manifest links, hostname metadata and Python syntax
were checked; the existing Vite server serves the new public files with their
expected MIME types. Workflow structure was reviewed, but a production build
and GitHub deployment were not run locally. Repository Pages settings, custom
domain, DNS CNAME and HTTPS setup are documented in `docs/GITHUB_PAGES.md`.

**Mass Properties editor (2026-11-16):** added a collapsible Editor panel
between ASW Editor and Beam Properties. It displays inspected total mass/CG
and edits individual Weight records: beam, attachment station, mass, jig
position and optional centroidal moments/products of inertia. Add, delete
and undo act on the ASW source automatically. Valid SI declarations display
kg, m and kg·m²; other files use consistent input units. The file's Constant
gravity converts force-weighted ASW mass/inertia fields, and products retain
ASW's negative-tensor-entry convention. Drag, volume and spin columns remain
intact. Source edits preserve comments, original tokens outside changed
fields, scale/add directives, optional zero defaults and multiple Weight
blocks. The existing inspection RPC validates each candidate before commit;
failed/stale edits cannot replace the applied model, and Save/Run wait for
pending edits. Six source/unit checks, three controller checks and five
responsive layout checks pass in the lightweight JavaScript harness. A
literal Daedalus pilot-weight edit changed one line and retained all other
records. Vite serves the modules; no browser, build or numerical solve ran.
Distributed beam mass remains editable under Beam Properties.

**Output controls cleanup (2026-11-16):** removed the Export results button
and Derivatives output pane, including their event handlers and rendering
code. Output retains Total Forces and Solver report; archived views selecting
Derivatives fall back to Solver report. Derivative calculation settings and
saved numerical data remain supported. Lightweight syntax and responsive
layout checks pass; no solver or browser was started.

**Compact Total Forces output (2026-11-16):** replaced the large lift readout
and vertically spaced metrics with aligned monospaced label/value columns,
following VibeLattice's Total Forces layout. The summary includes solved alpha,
beta, PG Mach, normalized stability-axis rates, force/moment coefficients,
Trefftz drag, profile drag, efficiency and declared controls. Control labels
come from the ASW beam/property metadata; file control settings are not
arbitrarily labeled degrees. Additional drag components and solver/structural
diagnostics are preserved in a closed disclosure. Columns adapt to panel
width. Five data/rendering tests and five responsive-layout tests pass in the
lightweight JavaScript harness; the existing Vite server serves the changes.

**Synchronized 2D animation (2026-11-16):** Bode and eigenmode phase, amplitude,
input, frequency and mode selection now update the common span-property plot
alongside the aircraft. Signed values use the saved equilibrium plus
`scale * (real*cos(phase) - imag*sin(phase))`; modal normalization matches the
selected body/Earth geometry. Full-cycle limits hold the vertical axes fixed,
and pointer/touch readouts retain their material location during playback.
Absolute stresses and strain bounds are formed from reconstructed signed
quantities rather than treating absolute values as linear responses. Force
per length includes the strip-length derivative. Additional flow, length,
axis-moment and shoulder outputs reuse the existing four physical output
snapshots without another solve. Old archives lacking a required derivative
show a gap/unavailable message instead of a motionless equilibrium curve;
initial-state spectra retain the base view. Twelve span/plot checks, four
controller/geometry checks and two Python output-format checks pass. Existing
frequency UI tests now reflect the previously removed prose and diagnostics.
The served kernel bundle includes the new output module. No browser, build,
WASM initialization or numerical solver was started for these UI changes;
ISAE completion counts are unchanged.

**Aircraft image downloads (2026-11-16):** added a download icon to the 3D
view. Paused views export a single-page PDF; active mode, Bode and time
playback record a looping GIF of the current camera view, up to 10 seconds.
GIF capture uses at most 640 pixels per side, targets 25 frames/s, sends one
frame at a time to a dedicated worker and caps encoded size at 16 MiB. The
button shows progress and cancels the export on a second click. Both WebGL
and software viewers copy freshly drawn pixels without changing the camera
or running the solver. Seven lightweight export tests and five layout tests
pass; independent PDF/GIF readers verified image colors, frame motion and
timing. Vite serves the new modules and worker. Browser rendering and full
build were not run in this resource-constrained session. The pinned MIT
gifenc 1.0.3 encoder, license and source map are in `web/vendor/gifenc/`.

removed result panel; old saved views targeting removed panels open the
Solver report. Lightweight layout and controller-settings checks pass.

Neither branch meets the predeclared extension gate or is adopted. A scalar
verifier checks 1,152 decisions and 192 finite-perturbation coefficients, plus
48 native scalar pairs at one equivalent input. The replay takes 0.39 seconds without new
aircraft solves; production and registered counts remain unchanged.

The [complete SA-6 roll/yaw table comparison](validation/isae-sa6-span-native-20261101.md)

The [main status table](validation/ISAE_STATUS.md) now leads with all 42 case entries;

Production sources and registered counts remain unchanged.

The [current SA-6 level-flight input comparison](validation/isae-sa6-level-input-comparison-20261101.md)
gives 220/220 matches across five configurations at the fixed source-inferred

The [SA-6 native-table reader](validation/isae-sa6-native-tables-20261101.md)

Ten source-reader tests pass. Reusing 1,122 old cached results yields 2,244

The [SA-6 saved-matrix precision audit](validation/isae-sa6-matrix-conditioning-20261101.md)

The numerical replay takes 1.66 seconds; no aircraft solve, browser or build is

The [SA-6 public-history audit](validation/isae-sa6-source-history-20261101.md)

The [continuous-wake browser control](validation/fourier-wake-ui-20261101.md)

The [continuous Fourier wake reference](validation/fourier-wake-nonparallel-20261101.md)

The 78-state replay takes 3.62 seconds without aerodynamic solves or field

The [SA-7 near-coplanar-wake diagnosis](validation/isae-sa7-near-coplanar-wake-20261101.md)

Exact integration of the retained piecewise-constant mutual terms isolates

The [SA-7 reported-node-count comparison](validation/isae-sa7-reported-node-count-20261101.md)

Independent fields, nonlinear residuals, section loads and wake forces verify

scalar, not a recovered native setup or complete reproduction. All 118 small

The [SA-7 efficiency-definition audit](validation/isae-sa7-efficiency-definition-20261101.md)

Using near-field efficiency, or carrying the existing mutual cores into wake
reporting, can bring the remaining checks inside 3%. The latter gives 406/406

The [SA-8 source follow-up](validation/isae-sa8-native-body-report-20261101.md)

The [SA-10 failure diagnostics](validation/isae-sa10-source-diagnostics-20261101.md)

The [SA-10 zero-incidence audit](validation/isae-sa10-zero-resolution-20261101.md)

The [SA-6 stall-width pilot](validation/isae-sa6-stall-width-20261101.md)

Neither variant qualifies for extension; production and all registered counts

Normal builds now skip the optional raw-validation download. Previously, the

I/O but does not establish the cause of the UserLAnd SSH disconnects. No solver,
Vite, browser-test or sub-agent process remains running at the latest check.
Automatic browser tests remain suspended, and ISAE counts are unchanged.

The [SA-8 drag-energy bound](validation/isae-sa8-drag-energy-bound-20261031.md)

No new nonlinear solves, production edits or registered gains; browser jobs
remain suspended.

The [SA-6 inertia-compatible mesh follow-up](validation/isae-sa6-inertia-mesh-rates-20261031.md)

The [SA-7 lift-force receiver audit](validation/isae-sa7-force-receivers-20261031.md)

The [SA-6 source-inertia follow-up](validation/isae-sa6-source-inertia-20261031.md)

The [SA-10 Louvered Fourier/refinement audit](validation/isae-sa10-louvered-basis-20261031.md)

The [SA-10 stall/junction follow-up](validation/isae-sa10-stall-junction-20261031.md)
completes all 162 states of three simpler models. With the later origin-CM

and maximum 5.80%, and strict zero-incidence force/efficiency checks. The

The [SA-8 body-volume follow-up](validation/isae-sa8-body-volume-20261031.md)

The [complete SA-8 strength-20 comparison](validation/isae-sa8-full-comparison-20261031.md)

The latest [stall-strength and local-force investigation](validation/isae-sa6-sa10-stall-strength-20261031.md)

The selected plan retains all four available families and the qualified

The [source and filament review](../artifacts/isae/sa4-source-geometry-review-20261030/README.md)

The [SA-4 endpoint-construction check](../artifacts/isae/sa4-endpoint-construction-20261030/README.md)
tests the documentation ambiguity at fixed circulation across all 84 saved

control-replay/algebra checks. All 168 altered configurations remain subsonic,
but none satisfies the original projected-residual gate. At the four failed

These are sensitivities, not corrected equilibria. No production change or

An independent finite-loop calculation passes 2,772 geometry/field/force
checks across the same 84 states, with maximum scaled field error 4.61e−12.
It evaluates 1,176 finite-segment operators and no new equilibrium solves.
The retained audit arrays also permit recovery of its report after a JSON
serialization failure, without repeating any kernel evaluations.

The [SA-4 adjacent-interval derivation](../artifacts/isae/sa4-adjacent-asymptotics-20261030/README.md)
identifies a generally nonzero curvature term proportional to strip length
in the symmetric bound-plus-longitudinal-wake force coefficient. It follows
from the documented chord-interpolated receiver. Uniform Glauert spacing
cancels the separate grading/sampling term, but not generally the curvature
term. Independent algebra agrees, including cancellation of the second
derivative of the quarter-chord offset. A finite accumulated contribution is
possible; the full global limit and native force treatment remain unproved.

All 84 saved states and 42 refinement pairs are retained. The saved-data
analysis passes 714 checks and shows approximately constant interior
coefficient/interval-length. The analytic geometry prediction passes 420
input/arithmetic checks; median interior coefficient errors against saved
operators decrease from 7.43% to 2.81% on the N18/36 drag-table pair and
1.46% to 0.979% on the N78/156 lift-table pair. These are two paired studies
with different angle lists, not four levels of the same state. The errors
measure the asymptotic model, not native reference agreement.
At N156, tip-inclusive coefficient errors remain 13.2–47.2%, with work errors
2.98–10.27%; all outliers are retained. No fitted constants, new aircraft
solves or production changes are involved. The candidate stays **562/588**.
An independent long-double kernel calculation passes all 62 predeclared
synthetic scenarios (496 two-interval evaluations), and a separate prediction
review passes 3,716 checks. These do not add native reference matches.
Removing the negative adjacent term would increase drag, worsening the
direction of the four remaining positive CD-table errors.
The subsequent [document review](../artifacts/isae/sa4-adjacent-asymptotics-20261030/adjacent-document-review.md)
finds no explicit adjacent-strip correction. Eq.155 specifies the force
receiver but leaves the bound-endpoint and self-influence conventions
insufficiently explicit. Current nodal endpoint offsets can put that receiver
off its straight bound segment; this geometry assumption remains to be checked.

The [SA-4 fixed-state vortex audit](../artifacts/isae/sa4-vortex-drag-decomposition-20261030/findings.md)
reconstructs the bound, semi-infinite-wake and infinite-wake operators for all
84 retained candidate states. The primary calculation passes 4,032 checks;
an independent scalar long-double Biot–Savart implementation passes 18,694
checks over all 672,840 receiver/source pairs. Both reproduce the saved
velocities and near-field/Trefftz drag, including exact-coordinate grouping
of signed wake strengths. There are 84 primary plus 84 independent prescribed-
circulation field evaluations, with zero nonlinear solves or new meshes.

The internal near-field/Trefftz gap splits exactly into positive bound work,
larger negative longitudinal-ray work, and a small half-infinite-wake
span-vector term. At the four failed CD-table states, different strips on
the same half supply 76.2–79.3% of that signed gap, own-strip terms supply
20.5–22.8%, and opposite halves supply 0.19–0.96%. Interior/interior pairs
account for 94.4–98.95%, using the predeclared outer 10% of each material-arc
half. These are signed algebraic partitions, not causal fractions or the
native total-CD discrepancy. The half-wake span-vector term is only
0.46–0.71% of the gap. The prior straight-wing same-half cancellation does
not apply to this curved mesh. This supports reviewing distributed force
integration, while providing no basis to remove an own-wake or bound term.
No kernel, default, reference or registered score changes; the candidate
remains **562/588**, with primary K40 local-flow limitations unresolved.

The subsequent [saved pair-separation analysis](../artifacts/isae/sa4-vortex-drag-decomposition-20261030/interpretation-review.md)
passes all 1,596 arithmetic checks across all 84 states without new fields or
solves. Adjacent strips alone contribute 71–73% of the internal near-field/
Trefftz gap at the four failed CD states, and 91–93% of its same-half
off-diagonal contribution. This behavior also occurs in passing states;
it does not identify the native total-CD error. The next mathematical
question is whether the documented adjacent-interval force sampling leaves
a leading contribution that persists under refinement. No source-backed
correction has yet been established; registered scores remain unchanged.

The [SA-4 saved-force decomposition](../artifacts/isae/sa4-drag-decomposition-20261030/findings.md)
reconstructs all 84 candidate states using the original scalar property tables

across all states and 42 mesh pairs. Maximum scaled strip-force differences
are 2.67e-15 in the primary reconstruction and 1.13e-14 in the audit. It performs no new flow,
residual, geometry or solver evaluations and leaves the candidate at **562/588**.
At the four remaining CD-table failures, Trefftz CDi contributes only
0.61–1.23 percentage points of the 3.07–3.19% total-CD error. The unidentified
CD−CDi remainder contributes the other 1.84–2.47 points (about 60–80%). Native
profile drag cannot be recovered separately from the seven archived outputs.

The curved-interval span-vector term is only 1.18–1.85% of the near-field/Trefftz
gap at those four states, so it is not the dominant contribution. Refinement
raises near-field circulation drag at the three N36 failures; at 10.098°,
reduced tangency drag dominates the N18→N36 total-CD decrease. In the primary
K40 lift polar, local residuals materially enter the Eq.70 tangency square:
at 7.06°/N156 its CD is 0.000559962, from leakage² 0.001230270 plus residual²
0.001089120 minus cross term 0.001759427. The full-rank CD-table residual terms
are instead at roundoff. These distinctions rule out treating all tangency drag
as stall leakage or substituting native CD−CDi for CDp. The next discriminator
is the unchanged-state bound/wake interaction decomposition; saved totals do
not contain those per-source operators. No physical formula, default, target
or registered score changes. The [component plot](../artifacts/isae/sa4-drag-decomposition-20261030/decomposition.svg)
retains all 84 states, including both zero-incidence points.

The primary truncated K40 states still have unresolved local flow. The native

The [SA-5 fixed-circulation junction audit](../artifacts/isae/sa5-dihedral-junction-20261028/report.json)
locates a remaining source-policy question at the sharp V-wing center. At

and 0.1206 from the wake. Independent finite-filament integration reproduces

shows a logarithmic singularity in this isolated integrated lift contribution
if the sharp junction retains nonzero continuous circulation as the cutoff
shrinks. This does not prove total-lift asymptotics, a coding defect, or ASWING's
historical corner treatment. No core, circulation, load law, or target changed;
the diagnostic needs no new equilibrium solve. Moving the lift force to an
interval centroid changes only Cm and cannot resolve the simultaneous force
differences.

## 2026-10-14 — Reusing system matrices for applied force and moment outputs

Bode now composes the six global applied force/moment output rows from its
owned physical matrices: C = W A + W_x R0 - C_support, Q = -W M, and D = W B.
The retained support matrix removes support loads from the nodal balances.
The position-dependent moment term remains even away from equilibrium;
internal beam loads and joint/ground reactions have exactly zero applied-load
partials. Initial-condition responses use the actual rate s X - x0 and do
not treat M x0 as a direct physical input. The matrices are immutable, bounded
to 2 MiB, and reused only for the same physical base and owned operators.
Unsupported controllers or changed wire/power-clipping branches retain the
original physical output path. Diagnostics count reuse within each sweep.

moments, complex scaling, ownership, fallback and repeated-sweep tests. The

788,837 numeric base/sample values (maximum
1.52e-07); A, M and the induced-field matrix G are
exactly unchanged. The full cold offline browser comparison passes across
794,364 values (maximum 1.44e-07),
with all original complete-equation residual, mobile plot, provenance and
export checks. The six output rows use 542,236 bytes on
DAE48. These are correctness checks, not an isolated runtime benchmark.
Earlier failed harness and cumulative-diagnostic attempts are preserved in
[the evidence bundle](validation/applied-load-matrices.json).

## 2026-10-12 — Bode setup comparison with Drela

The Bode implementation is **not confirmed equivalent to ASWING's setup or
discrete equations**. The descriptor equation and derivative signs agree with
Drela's unsteady theory, sections 13.1–13.2. That document explicitly reuses
Jacobians available from the converged Newton solve. OpenSwing still constructs
a new dynamic tangent. The current implementation shares circulation and complete geometry derivative
assembly with the nonlinear solvers, but still constructs a fresh tangent at
the dynamic base, with numerical differences for geometry fields and other
state columns and selected independent columns grouped.
Sparse storage and LU do not eliminate that work.

The existing released DAE profile (8 intervals per beam, 21 frequencies, four
inputs) attributes 1.89 seconds to all harmonic solves, 76.93 to dynamic
linearization, 51.57 to base construction, 47.88 to output recovery, and 14.90
to input derivatives, out of 195.10 seconds total. These are cumulative timings
for separate top-level stages from the earlier run, not a new benchmark or a
full-mesh timing. The dominant remaining work is model construction and recovery.

The browser defaults to a fixed aircraft frame, all controls plus a gust, and
0.1–100 rad/input T. Drela's published DAE plot displays rudder (Flap 3) response
over 0.1–10 cycles/s, including nonzero aircraft yaw rate, roll rate, sideslip and
bank. The fixed-frame default cannot reproduce those flight responses. The plot
does not provide its complete operating point, constraints, mesh or solver
settings; loading the same .asw geometry alone does not reproduce that case.
ASWING's manual does compute all declared controls together, so that behavior
is not a mismatch; gusts are enabled separately. Frame constraints must be chosen
for the physical experiment, separately from steady trim constraints.

Other differences remain: OpenSwing uses an objective SO(3) midpoint beam
discretization, and its Bode tangent includes aerodynamic geometry feedback.
Drela's steady theory section 4.6 describes lagging selected influence terms
during Newton iterations to retain a narrow structural block. Removing those
terms permanently from a frequency-response tangent would change its equations;
the steady iteration shortcut is not by itself an accuracy justification.
Pointwise circulation is a documented ASWING option, although Drela describes
Fourier circulation as more efficient; OpenSwing defaults to pointwise values.

The audit and source references are in
`docs/validation/bode-drela-setup-audit.json`. Its source hashes describe the
audited version before the derivative-sharing changes below. Complete Jacobian
reuse and a reproducible flight-response comparison remain unfinished.

validation load. The unmodified 48-panel runs were stopped while stalled and
are not completed baseline timings.

## Current source

- `openswing/frozen_influence.py`: owned jig-geometry vortex/volume coefficients, material receiver geometry and bounded cache with Mach/core/image-plane invalidation.

- `openswing/gust_file.py`: verified straight type-5 numeric gust import/export,
  common-field validation and explicit rejection of unmapped legacy parameters.
- `openswing/custom_constraints.py`: bounded custom equations at the physical trial,
  loaded target continuation and local rank/one-sided tangent checks.
- `web/custom-constraints.js`: equation/sensor editor and custom trim reports.

- `openswing/asw.py`: source-preserving ASW parser, global records, units, per-variable
  symmetry, piecewise cubic interpolation and explicit discontinuity sides.
- `openswing/asw_edit.py`: lossless/canonical serialization, transactional distribution
  edits, stale-spline guards and actual-spline plots.
- `web/distribution-editor.js`: station editing, preview/apply/undo and draft protection.
- `web/frequency-data.js` and `web/frequency-comparison.js`: shared complex-response
  extraction, simultaneous input/output/station comparisons and CSV/SVG exports.
- `openswing/geometry.py`: arc-length mesh and local section frames, geometry export.
- `openswing/sensors.py`: moving pylon axes, local airflow, inertial/GPS and
  structural measurements, trace/sample metadata and angle singularities.
- `openswing/feedback.py`: measurement/error/integral gain laws, scheduled gains,
  nonlinear actuator equations and custom state rates, consistent startup and
  local tangent guards.
- `openswing/control_expressions.py`: bounded scalar syntax-tree evaluation,
  lazy conditional branches and one-sided composite-residual slope checks.
- `openswing/steady_feedback.py`: simultaneous controller/operating equilibrium,
  command trim variables, target continuation and full final tangent rank check.
- `openswing/control_tables.py`: original .con blocks with explicit channel/unit
  bindings; no guessed INDEXC mapping.
- `openswing/body_shoulders.py`: concentric radius-jump geometry and exact
  area integration of the radius-dependent source core.
- `openswing/frequency_sweep.py`: transactional sample refinement, owned frozen
  frequency models and source/settings-bound local continuation handles.
- `openswing/flow_survey.py`: arbitrary body/Earth planes, saved-state inspection,
  field decomposition, current-body/ground masks and portable sampling results.
- `web/flow-results.js`: selected-state surveys, quiver/color plots and CSV/JSON/SVG.
- `openswing/aero.py`: lifting-line residual and loads on supplied geometry,
  with optional elastic motion, empirical circulation lag and rate lift.
- `openswing/circulation.py`: material sine-series coordinates, weighted flow
  equations, strict physical-state encoding and per-beam pointwise/Fourier mixing.
- `openswing/trefftz.py`: far-wake force/drag quadrature, image planes, explicit
  diagnostic gaps and separate near-field accounting.
- `openswing/structure.py`: independent geometrically exact clamped/free spatial beam
  BVP; coupled section compliance and exact rigid limits.
- `openswing/equilibrium_state.py`: portable physical steady-state packets, exact
  source/mesh compatibility, rescaling, trim/controller restoration and full-load
  Newton correction with final tangent checks.
- `openswing/network.py`: mixed SO(3) connected-beam mounted equilibrium with
  gravity, inertia, pylons, rigid/pinned/roller/sprung constraints, simultaneous circulation,
  operating unknowns and conservative load transfer. Dense numerical Jacobian with load continuation.
- `openswing/inertia.py`: body-motion acceleration fields, transformed point inertia
  and spin, distributed inertia, real/apparent spatial matrices and added-mass loads.
- `openswing/local_motion.py`: analytic derivatives of SO(3) section interpolation,
  moving-frame/pylon accelerations, material strain rate and nodal load transfer.
- `openswing/time_initialization.py`: exact saved steady launch, zero-local-rate
  consistency check, mixed frame targets, released trim constraints and preserved
  controller commands.
- `openswing/time_state.py`: physical time checkpoints, controller/forcing
  references, BDF history, validation and exact-state continuation.
- `openswing/time_integration.py`: coupled BDF1/BDF2 elastic/circulation/frame
  integration, prescribed/free/mixed motion, initial equilibrium and load
  release, Newton recovery, event steps and progress callbacks.
- `openswing/linear_dynamics.py`: continuous descriptor chart/residual, fixed,
  prescribed, free and mixed loaded bases, exact coordinate-integrator factors,
  physical complex outputs/state scaling, constraint reduction and dense/Arnoldi
  eigenmodes with full left/right vectors.
- `openswing/frequency_response.py`: full complex descriptor solve, conditioned LU,
  flap/engine and spatial harmonic gust partials, direct output feedthrough, pole
  gaps, frequency-dependent forcing metadata and matched broken-loop ratios.
- `openswing/stability.py`: operating-point spectra, fixed-metric shape tracking,
  explicit gaps and checked instability brackets with full point records.
- `openswing/reduced_model.py`: selected real modes, mass-dual projection,
  checked algebraic input lift, physical output matrices and full comparisons.
- `openswing/rom_file.py`: annotated complex ROM tables, literal coefficient
  preservation, real realization, time-unit reconciliation and SI export.
- `openswing/forcing.py`: documented time-table parsing and piecewise cubic
  sampling, scaling/relative settings, actuator, acceleration and active net-load
  channels, doubled-time/end events and explicit unsupported-channel errors.
- `openswing/dynamic_inertia.py`: eight-point distributed material-mass integration,
  elastic inertial/gyroscopic loads and virtual-power-consistent transfer.
- `openswing/damping.py`: energy/passivity diagnostic for coupled componentwise
  material damping; retains rather than alters the documented constitutive law.
- `openswing/operating.py`: flow/motion/control unknowns paired with force, moment,
  lift or coefficient targets; engine-power unknowns, free-flight acceleration preset
  and target continuation.
- `openswing/propulsion.py`: proportional/disk/P-factor engine loads, physical
  power branch and conserving jet profiles; current pylon positions/axes.
- `openswing/struts.py`: bilateral or tension-only axial law, slack/preload and energy.
- `openswing/joints.py`: validated Joint/Jangle binding, normalized axes,
  continuous piecewise natural cubic moment-angle laws, breaks/extrapolation.
- `openswing/recovery.py`: current-frame section loads, translated moments,
  mechanical strains/curvature changes, signed shell-point strain, strain bound
  and closed-shell torsional stress, missing-data flags and unit metadata.
- `openswing/derivatives.py`: centered implicit residual linearization; single
  factorization, rank/conditioning/residual diagnostics, load/acceleration and
  structural responses in explicit units and base axes; closed-loop equilibrium
  states, command columns and physical controller/measurement responses.
- `openswing/kinematics.py`: physical velocity/acceleration at separate file reference
  points, rotating-frame velocity derivatives, Euler rates and turn relations.
- `openswing/atmosphere.py`: US76 lower-atmosphere hydrostatic layers and
  geometric/geopotential conversion; scaled file-unit air properties and reports.
- `openswing/volume.py`: body and point source/doublet influence, slender-body
  lift/profile/apparent loads, eight-point element quadrature and explicit cores.
- `openswing/ground.py`: Earth/body rotation, physical image-plane reflection,
  current-geometry clearance and ground metadata. Vortex images live in
  `aero.py`; source/doublet images live in `volume.py`.
- `openswing/bridge.py`: shared native/browser JSON interface.
- `web/`: three-column workbench, jig/deformed 3D views, ASW editor, rigid/constrained analysis,
  motion/target/engine editors, brace/body-mass choices, circular bodies,
  pylons/struts/propeller disks, Earth pose/image-plane inputs and rendering,
  mass/CG/inertia, lift/force plots, reactions and downloads;
  browser worker executes the Python kernel under Pyodide.
- `web/time-results.js`: open-loop time controls, time-series plotting and CSV,
  snapshot playback, body/Earth geometry transformation; `main.js` synchronizes
  snapshot metrics, distributions and full-history JSON.
- `scripts/prepare.mjs`: stages original sources/examples and checksum-verified
  numerical runtime; generates the downloadable original-source archive.
- `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`: full-scope requirement and verification gaps.

## Verified evidence so far

- Native tests: 269 passed in the full suite (572.68 s). This includes all three official
  example input parsers (Daedalus, ultralight sailplane, flying wing).
- Native suites cover parsing, analytic vortex integrals, symmetry, ellipse lift
  and drag, mesh convergence, control sign, stall, compressibility, speed scaling,
  exact circular arcs, linear beam limits, coupled compliance and covariance.
- Network tests add large-rotation mesh refinement, independent BVP comparison,
  connected beams, all implemented joint types, rigid offsets, gravity reactions,
  mechanisms/redundancy, coupled rigid limits and deformed load balance.
- Inertia and operating checks include kinetic energy and frame/reference
  invariance, point-cloud equivalence through nonlinear deformation, uniform-rod
  inertia/torque, centrifugal/gyroscopic loads, flat-plate added mass, Newton–Euler
  free-flight accelerations, inverse speed/alpha/control and coupled-state recovery.
- Propulsion checks add ideal hover thrust, forward power budget, windmilling branch,
  direct polar integration of jet linear/angular momentum, and P-factor derivatives
  from independent radial/azimuthal blade-element quadrature for either spin.
  Inverse power and specified surface lift exclude direct point/engine forces.
  Brace checks include energy gradient, covariance, exact parallel stiffness,
  preload, slack, superposition, removal of mechanisms and pylon/support balance.
- Volume checks add independent singularity potential derivatives, adaptive field
  quadrature, PG/coordinate/parameter invariance, cylinder drag and pressure-based
  added mass, closed-body Munk moment, pod symmetry, body-only equilibrium and

## Deployment

The exact Sites project is persisted in `.openai/hosting.json`. Do not create
another project. It was created owner-private, and no audience change has been
requested. Source and runtime are packaged and deployed with the Sites skill.
The authoritative live URL returned by the successful native deployment is
`https://openswing.sanctity.chatgpt.site`. Sanitized source/deployment metadata
is retained in ignored `.sites-runtime/deployment.json`. The creation-time
expected URL differed; do not use it in place of the actual deployment URL.
Use the native Site's current version/deployment state as the authoritative hosted
status. Do not repeat creation or deployment merely from this record.

## Environment details

Python is `python3`; a project venv exists at `.venv`. Native validation versions:
Python 3.14.4, NumPy 2.5.3, SciPy 1.18.1, pytest 9.1.1. Browser runtime is Pyodide
314.0.7, Python 3.14.2, NumPy 2.4.6, SciPy 1.18.0. npm dependencies are installed.

The default Playwright install does not support Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64. Its Ubuntu
24.04 ARM64 browser ZIP downloaded successfully, but the Node ZIP extraction
stalled. The verified existing ZIP was extracted with Python, and the stalled
installer was explicitly terminated. Chromium is at
`/tmp/aswing-chromium/chrome-linux/chrome`. Missing system shared libraries were
downloaded as Ubuntu packages and extracted locally (no system packages changed)
to `/tmp/aswing-browser-libs/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu`. Run browser tests here as:

```sh
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/aswing-browser-libs/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu \
OPENSWING_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/tmp/aswing-chromium/chrome-linux/chrome \
npm run test:browser
```

The dev server binds loopback because this host denies network-interface
enumeration required for Vite's wildcard-host address display. External hosting
uses the static production build and is independent of this local restriction.

Reference PDFs/text and official example inputs are in ignored `.reference/`;
upstream SHA-256/fetch metadata can be generated with `scripts/fetch-references.py`.
They must not be accidentally included in the project's MIT-licensed source ZIP.

Ground images now work for the implemented steady singularities. Retain the
explicit oblique-compressible approximation marker and investigate the upstream
transformed-plane convention with independent reference results. Free-surface
images are the linearized constant-pressure model, not a wave solver. Jets and

exact node/zero-length-interval handling and comprehensive nonplanar/wake-coupling
parity, sprung-hinge interior moment traces/offset passivity and undocumented ASWING compression behavior.

of attack, Mach=0 and body −z gravity. At 12/24/48 panels, CL is
0.414246364 / 0.406546578 / 0.404337435 and maximum displacement is
2.220226666 / 2.260675161 / 2.268004116 m. From 24 to 48 panels the changes are

published ASWING or experimental validation.

The native host benefits greatly from `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` for these small
dense systems. Initial rigid-limit root failures were traced to relative-only
finite differences disappearing on addition to jig coordinates. The supplied
Jacobian now uses scaled absolute perturbations; regression tests cover rigid
gravity and offset-joint loads at every continuation step.

`docs/validation/powered-braced.json`, using 3000 W per propeller, wire braces,

exact attachment insertion. CL is 0.499590871 / 0.482849902 / 0.477885411;
maximum displacement is 1.297422443 / 1.346899990 / 1.350062781 m. The last
refinement changes CL by 1.04%, displacement by 0.23%, and net CD by 2.38%.
The narrow jets need spatial resolution; these are internal sensitivity results,
not ASWING or experimental validation. Shaft power 1500 W at the specified RPM
is below the modeled viscous loss and correctly gives windmilling drag; the
powered browser/WASM checks therefore use 3000 W.

Structural mass/stiffness now sample the material arc midpoint; aerodynamic
quantities retain the Glauert-angle midpoint. The new mesh-study values reflect

The fuselage frame uses its documented reversed Euler sequence (steady eq. 10),
which matters for inclined bodies and their inertia/centroid axes.

`CG_Calc.pdf` was fetched directly from the MIT documentation path and its
SHA-256 is in the ignored reference manifest. The web PDF extractor could not
open it; local PDF text extraction confirmed equation 29, including negative
off-diagonal signs for ASW product-of-inertia inputs. No reference PDF is shipped.

The operating target continuation initializes from the quantities at the supplied
initial state, then ramps to the requested targets along with structural loading.
The aero cache includes operating unknown bytes so motion/control changes cannot
reuse stale circulation influence/load evaluations.

Engine control settings are in input power units for types 1/2 and gain-defined
units for type 0. Shared Keng indices set every corresponding engine. Surface
circulation and engine inflow/jet effects share the nonlinear residual. Engines
do not see other engines' jets, following the documented modeling choice. Negative
Rdisk disables jet effects; a zero thrust-axis vector defaults to forward thrust.
The type 2 sign convention is independently validated by blade-element integration.

Struts are passive supports: their stiffness remains in the unloaded tangent,
while dLo preload/slack is continued. Support totals include fixed anchors; physical
operating force targets exclude brace forces. The selected bilateral/wire law is
exported. Full ASWING strut compression parity is not claimed.

PyMuPDF 1.28.2 was installed only into the local development venv to inspect
equation images from the ignored reference PDFs. It is not a runtime dependency
and no reference pages or rendered reference images are shipped.

Body strips have null circulation/lift coefficients and carry forces, moments
and physical lengths. Only lifting segments introduce circulation unknowns;
body-only models solve without dummy aerodynamic states. `panels` counts all
beam segments, while `lifting_panels` counts the circulation variables. Total
apparent force includes both bodies and surfaces; the indirect surface-lift
constraint uses only the surface apparent contribution when removing that load.

The body radius is integrated with eight-point Gauss quadrature per current
straight interval. Radius jumps requiring shoulder loads remain explicit errors.
No end-cap source or undocumented thick-wing cross-sectional area is invented.
Point drag area now also produces its source field, in addition to point volume's
doublet. Both fields follow deformed pylons; the 3D view includes their pylon lines.

Hinge tests include analytic serial rigid links, a nonlinear pendulum/spring

## Atmosphere and lift-factor increment

`altitude_m` is a prescribed geometric altitude in metres, independent of Earth Z
and model length units. The US76 lower-atmosphere equations cover −5 to 86 km,
including geopotential conversion, all seven molecular-temperature layers and
the small kinetic-temperature correction above 80 km. File sea-level density
and sound speed provide the input-unit scaling. A density override takes
precedence; a fixed PG Mach remains separate from ambient/local Mach. Gravity
magnitude rotates with attitude but leaves original weight-to-mass conversion
unchanged. Equivalent-airspeed and dynamic-pressure targets can solve true speed;
N multiplies only the specified lift target. Exact ASWING VIAS conversion and
table interpolation/range still need upstream evidence.

`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python scripts/verify-atmosphere.py` writes
`docs/validation/atmosphere-and-targets.json`. The flexible example uses 8 panels,
30 m/s equivalent airspeed, N=1.5 times 1000 N specified lift, gravity 4 m/s²
and PG Mach=0. At 0/10/20 km, solved true speed is 30 / 51.635206225 /
111.356110093 m/s and alpha is 2.281397748 / 2.302842538 / 2.425476042 deg.
The small shape/alpha change at equal dynamic pressure reflects the implemented
local section-moment Mach correction, which retains actual sound speed even
when global PG Mach is fixed at zero. Residuals are below 2e-11. This is internal
coupled validation; it is not a comparison with ASWING's executable.

Native atmosphere checks use COESA Table I values and an independent ODE
integration of geometric-height hydrostatic equilibrium, plus layer continuity,
unit scaling, density/added-mass/local-Mach scaling, Earth-Z independence,
gravity/mass separation, and indirect speed/lift target recovery. The NASA
report is fetched separately by `scripts/fetch-references.py` and remains outside
the MIT source archive.

## Steady flight-trim increment

`kinematics.py` resolves aircraft velocity at the velocity reference, acceleration
at the separate acceleration reference, the body-origin motion, and the rotating
body-frame velocity derivative. The radial Earth-component target follows the
user guide's `AY - UX WZ`; its exact ASWING convention for separated reference
points remains unverified. The complete vector relation uses the same material
point consistently. Euler rates use the documented rotation sequence and become
null at the elevation pole while vector kinematics remain available.

`steady_turn_constraints()` generates ten kinematic equations, or sixteen when
three flap IDs (roll/pitch/yaw) and an engine ID are supplied for six-load trim.
The browser obtains the presets from the same Python helper, validates control
IDs, and displays the editable target list. Draft preset fields do not affect an
existing result until applied. Speed and sideslip stay prescribed; beta=0 gives
coordinated flight. Control authority, travel limits and equilibrium stability
are not inferred. These are local steady states at prescribed air properties,
not time integration or trajectory-following wakes.

The original `examples/trim-aircraft.asw` has an elastic main wing, elevator,
aileron, rudder, proportional thrust, a point mass with full diagonal inertia,
and distinct velocity/acceleration references. Its tail and fin connect to the
main-wing root via rigid pylons. It is an implementation demonstrator, not a
calibrated real aircraft.

## Coupled derivative increment

`linearize_equilibrium()` releases the original inverse/trim constraints at a
converged state and differentiates the complete implemented nonlinear residual.
Fixed-acceleration responses retain prescribed accelerations. Free-flight
responses replace operating equations with six zero-net-load constraints and
solve acceleration responses with controls otherwise held fixed. These are
quasi-steady elastic responses, without local elastic velocities, unsteady
circulation or flutter. Centered partial derivatives, a single column-scaled LU
factorization, SVD conditioning and linear-residual checks support all requested
columns. Wire, Jangle-slope and engine-clipping transitions are rejected when a
unique tangent is not established.

Standard fractional-speed, radian-angle and normalized stability-axis rate
columns coexist with dimensional body-velocity/rate bases at either the file
velocity reference or body origin, and flap/engine columns in file setting
units. Dimensional wrenches use body axes and the file moment reference.
Distributed beam aerodynamic coefficients exclude direct point-object, engine
and apparent-mass loads, while separate total-fluid and net matrices retain
those effects. Output coefficient axes and dynamic-pressure/reference-length
normalization stay fixed at the base state. Reference/origin accelerations,
nodal displacement/incremental rotation, element loads and circulation are
exported, with structural responses plotted in the browser.

## Section strain and torsional stress increment

`recovery.py` reuses the full section compliance and the nonlinear residual's
current material-midpoint frame. It exports local c/s/n force/moment, bending
moments at the tension axis, torque at the elastic axis, mechanical strains,
curvature changes relative to the jig, axial strain at the tension axis, signed
shell-point strain and the absolute-contribution strain bound. Closed-shell
torsion uses `Ms_prime/(2 Atshell)` with both signed and absolute outputs.
No normal stress, transverse-shear flow, warping or strength margin is invented
from the available data. Infinite stiffness gives zero strain while finite shell
geometry can still carry nonzero stress.

Missing Cshell/Nshell gives null shell strain; a single declared coordinate
uses zero for the other. Zero Atshell means missing, negative means invalid;
both give null stress without changing equilibrium. The theory's tension-axis
shell coordinates are explicit because the user-guide labels instead reference
the elastic axis. The printed repeated jig-curvature subscript is interpreted
using the constitutive curvature changes, so unloaded curved beams remain
strain-free. These documented ambiguities need independent executable evidence.

`elements[].t` and derivative `element_order[].t` now label the actual material
midpoint (`mesh.ts`); previous exports used the aerodynamic collocation parameter
(`mesh.tm`). The derivative study was regenerated and all numerical matrices,
base values and diagnostics were verified identical, with only those coordinate
labels changing.

The original `examples/stress-wing.asw` adds illustrative shell dimensions to
the flexible wing. `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python scripts/verify-sections.py`

## Instantaneous unsteady residual increment

The shared residual accepts four local nodal fields `(u,w,udot,wdot)` plus
circulation rates. Section/pylon motion includes Coriolis acceleration and the
absolute-angular-acceleration transport term `Omega cross w`. Direct Earth-frame
trajectory differentiation verifies the convention; the printed rotational
inertia equations omit that explicit term, so executable parity is not claimed.
Local airflow now includes beam, body, point-object and engine motion. P-factor
uses actual mount rotation. Volume and propulsion wakes remain quasi-steady.

Distributed real mass uses eight Gauss points with the exact derivatives of the
chosen interpolated geometry. There is no duplicated finite-segment inertia.
Real-mass and fluid sample loads transfer through transpose velocity maps, giving
the correct virtual power. The complete real/apparent acceleration operator is
symmetric and positive semidefinite in tested deformed wing/body cases, and its
six-DOF rigid reduction matches the independent spatial tensors. The real-mass
operator also matches a directly differentiated kinetic-energy history.
These facts do not establish conservation of the complete finite-rotation
strong-form beam/aeroelastic discretization.

The documented `e + D edot = S load` law uses tdeps for extension/bending and
tdgam for shear/torsion. Geometry, not total viscoelastic load, supplies reported
mechanical strain. An energy-coordinate diagnostic detects nonpassive coupled
sections with unequal times; it does not silently change the input damping law.

Circulation tangency includes `-(2/pi) gamma_dot/Vperp`, and the accompanying
rate lift acts at quarter chord. Lag-adjusted pressure drag avoids introducing
artificial stall drag. Rate force/moment and `CDrate` are separate from the steady
circulation contribution and its near-field efficiency estimate.

`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python scripts/verify-unsteady.py` generates
`docs/validation/unsteady-residual.json`, retaining hashes for the script and
all 21 kernel modules. The verification-only descriptor pencil gives:

| Panels | First undamped frequency [rad/s] | First root with tdeps=0.02 s [1/s] |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 4 | 6.271931838 | −0.393371290 + 6.259583693 i |
| 8 | 6.232384971 | −0.388426224 + 6.220269086 i |
| 16 | 6.219900693 | −0.386871646 + 6.207857518 i |

For L=2 m, EI=100 N m² and mass density 2 kg/m, the analytic frequency is
6.215495598 rad/s and the analytic damped root is
−0.386323855 + 6.203478009 i per second. The 16-panel relative errors are 0.07087%
and 0.07101%; eigenpair residuals are below 4e-17. The actual lifting-line
residual/lift gives the documented rational transfer `(1+2ik)/(1+4ik)` to a
maximum absolute error of 1.053e-5 across k=0.001–100 at aspect ratio 200,000.
This approximation is not exact Theodorsen theory. The study does not provide
general aeroelastic modes, a flutter solver, time integration, or ASWING/
experimental validation.

The steady entry points retain their previous mass and nodal load discretization.
Passing elastic-motion fields selects the consistent unsteady transfer, including
at zero rate. Future dynamic initialization must use that residual consistently.
Unsteady trajectory and flight-state kinematics, gusts, time convergence,
general eigenmodes/flutter, sensors, control laws and the rest of the requirements
ledger remain open; the browser does not expose a time-response solver yet.


## Implicit time kernel and local launch increment

The experimental `solve_time` API and worker `action="time"` now integrate the
coupled elastic/circulation/frame equations with BDF1/BDF2. Initial equilibrium
uses the unsteady residual; nodal load release is available. Both prescribed
frame accelerations and free-flight six-load constraints evolve position,
orientation and velocity. SO(3) increments, reference-point transport and default
Earth gravity remain consistent. Damped Newton can reuse its tangent, halves
failed steps and caps subsequent growth; no time-error estimator is implied.

The new native tests cover temporal order against exact axial oscillation,
rotated free fall, torque-free energy/angular momentum, rotation branches,
reference-point kinematics, loaded aeroelastic equilibrium and independent
Newton/Euler balances in free aerodynamic motion. The workbench time controls,
forcing histories, gusts, restart and full modes/flutter remain open. Historical
instantaneous-residual notes above describe the preceding increment.

`npm start` now builds and serves at http://127.0.0.1:8000. The build also creates
`dist/openswing-local.zip`, downloadable as Local app from hosted workbenches.
The ZIP includes the runtime, kernel, fonts, examples and source archive. After
extraction it runs with `python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1`, with no
Node.js or scientific Python installation needed. The Python server only serves
static files. Source builds require Node.js and standard-library Python for
packaging; native scientific dependencies are needed only for validation.

## Open-loop forcing and time workbench increment

`forcing.py` implements the documented open-loop text format for declared flap
and engine settings plus prescribed-frame linear/angular accelerations. It
handles comments, column scaling, relative initial settings, natural cubic
segments and doubled-time jumps/slope breaks. It rejects unknown/sensor/inverse
channels, unavailable actuators, uncovered time intervals and accelerations
conflicting with free flight. Natural spline endpoint parity remains unverified.

Every trial residual uses the current prescribed values. Integration lands on
knots, saves left-hand states at doubled times and restarts BDF1 after each
break. This avoids premature force application. Progress callbacks report actual
accepted times. Tests include independent cubic translation, degree-based
angular acceleration, free proportional-thrust dynamics, a non-grid-aligned
step, actual section pitching loads and integrated high-AR circulation/rate lift.

`scripts/verify-time.py` and `docs/validation/time-forcing.json` retain the input
models, source hashes, histories and exact comparison formulas. The velocity
errors for both ramp trajectories fall by approximately four on each halving
of dt. The step's velocity error is 4.76e-13 m/s. The empirical-lag lift ramp has
maximum CL errors 5.133e-6, 1.489e-6 and 4.098e-7 at dt=.02/.01/.005 s. These are
independent model/time-order checks, not ASWING executable or experimental parity.

The workbench exposes nonlinear time response, prescribed/free frame modes,
forcing text import/export and a pulse helper. History plots show coefficients,
motion, node response and inputs. Scrub/play selects actual accepted snapshots
and synchronizes metrics, loads, section recovery and the solver report.
Earth view transforms beam/pylon vertices with the stored position and rotation;
its physical image plane stays at Earth zero. Both renderers preserve the camera
during playback. The browser environment exercised the software fallback; the
Earth transform also has an independent known-rotation check.

History JSON retains all physical snapshots and the full original solve request;
history CSV retains actual times, step/order and forcing side. Span/section CSVs
identify the selected snapshot time. Editing inputs invalidates the whole history
and stops playback. Cancel terminates the worker, then reloads a fresh runtime.
The original `examples/transient-wing.asw` adds a uniform flap and equal 0.02-s
damping times to the shell wing; its parameters are illustrative, not calibrated.

## Earth-coordinate gust increment

`openswing/gust.py` defines uniform, compact one-minus-cosine, indefinite
sinusoidal, arithmetic-expression and superposed Earth-coordinate fields.
Expressions are interpreted through a restricted numeric AST, with explicit
schema/size/finite-value checks. No user code is executed. The JSON schema is an
OpenSwing extension; the legacy numeric `.gust` catalog is explicitly rejected.
Public user/theory documents and sample input data were consulted, not the
ASWING solver source. Numeric catalog/sign conventions remain a requirement.

Every aerodynamic velocity site samples the field at its current deformed
location transformed by the aircraft Earth pose: lifting control, force and
axis points, body quadrature, engines and point-object pylons. This participates
in the common residual, including operating derivatives and implicit time steps.
A gust does not directly change aircraft velocity or real inertial mass. The
reported coefficients and source/wake references keep the still-atmosphere
convention. Gust-relative operating/sensor conventions remain open. The existing
published apparent-mass velocity/rate terms include gust velocity, but there is
no extra fluid pressure-gradient acceleration term or exact Sears transfer.
These limitations are retained in rigid, coupled and time-state reports.

Cosine/sinusoid time steps check actual sample-point phase travel, including
outside the pulse support, and retry if it exceeds pi/8. Accepted travel caps
subsequent step growth. This prevents a monotonic coarse step from entirely
skipping a narrow pulse, but is not error control or a general expression-event
locator. The retry count is exported separately. All fields still require
spatial and temporal refinement.

The browser supplies common field controls, arbitrary expression components,
custom/summed JSON import/export, and a profile preview using the actual WASM
field evaluator. Preview ranges/components preserve an existing analysis;
changes to the physical field invalidate it. Time histories/CSV expose body-axis
gust velocity at the velocity reference; the report records Earth/body samples
and the actual field time. JSON includes the field and all load-sample positions.
The original `examples/vertical-cosine.gust.json` and README provide a runnable
elastic-wing demonstration. At 4 panels/beam, V=10, alpha=0, H=3, amplitude=1,
duration=1.3 and dt=.02 it completed 65 accepted steps, no retries, maximum
residual 9.045e-9 and displacement range .003624–.200613 input L. These values
are an illustrative workflow check, not aircraft calibration or convergence.

The independent native checks include axial dynamic-pressure scaling with fixed
reference normalization, spatially integrated body drag, offset engine/pylon
sampling, Earth-pose covariance, distinct wing control/force samples, exact
elastic-position feedback, a narrow frozen pulse and temporal-gust lag
refinement. An additional free-flight axial-drag case checks the exact velocity
law with second-order refinement and the correct acceleration/force balance.
`scripts/verify-gust.py` / `docs/validation/gust-response.json` preserve source
hashes, complete input models/conditions, formulas, histories and errors.
The temporal-gust CL errors are 6.449702e-7, 1.871077e-7, 5.149653e-8 at
steps .02/.01/.005. The elastic-feedback tip is 2.333527813434408 input L,
matching its analytic root to reported precision. The narrow pulse requested a
single step but took 65; maximum point-force error was 1.31e-14 input F.

The full user goal remains active. Remaining work includes sensors/control laws,
all numeric gust types and companion formats, general coupled eigenmodes/flutter,
Bode/ROM workflows, restart, remaining geometry/constraint conventions and
published reference validation, as tracked in REQUIREMENTS.md.

## Coupled eigenmode increment (2026-10-04)

`openswing/linear_dynamics.py` adds the continuous common-residual pencil, loaded
fixed/free-flight bases, vacuum, hidden-constraint reduction, dense and
shift-and-invert finite roots, full left/right vectors and physical complex
outputs. Nodal spatial rotation increments and published Euler frame kinematics
retain actual nonzero base drift. Both reference-point conventions and the
existing common real/apparent inertia, lag, damping, propulsion, ground and gust
terms participate. Base controls are fixed after trim. Matrices and vector
scaling/layout are optionally exported through the new `modes` bridge action.

A right-space constraint staircase plus QR range projection avoids singular-M
inversion and numerical infinite-root classification. Left vectors are recovered
from matched full-pencil generalized Schur vectors, with null-space fallback and
full residual checks. Repeated/defective zero pairs can be non-normalizable.
Constraint thresholds account for weak-derivative amplification of basis error;
near-cutoff derivatives in the *original* pencil trigger a refinement error.
Projected singular values are reported separately because they contain propagated
roundoff (including native/WASM differences). Geometry differences are fourth
order. This is a numerical experimental solver, not a proof of mode completeness;
mesh, tangent and rank studies are necessary.

`web/mode-results.js` adds mode settings, complex root map/selection, body/Earth
linear phase playback, local displacements/rotations, complex strip/section
loads/strain/stress, root/output CSV and full JSON. Ordinary coefficient, loading
and Structure panes retain the base solution. Display amplitude is arbitrary,
phase playback holds it fixed, and saved solver data are immutable. Vacuum
preserves file mass and the selected Earth gravity magnitude. Engine blocks in
vacuum are explicitly rejected.

`tests/test_modes.py` covers hidden constraints, full original-pencil equations,
physical mass normalization, weak-inertia rejection, dense/Arnoldi selection,
exact oscillator roots, mixed time units, cantilever mesh order, twelve vacuum
rigid-body states, gyroscopic nutation/intermediate-axis instability, unsteady
circulation decay, complex constitutive outputs, vacuum JSON and nonsmooth
wire/Jangle tangents. The heave/pitch file and `scripts/modal-benchmark.py` are
original inputs/equations, not recovered ASWING source. The larger source-hashed
study is `scripts/verify-modes.py` → `docs/validation/coupled-modes.json`.

Native and browser verification details and final study numbers are recorded
below after the final run. Earlier regression/artifact counts describe their
own source versions; the full requirement ledger remains authoritative.

## Forced harmonic response increment (2026-10-04)

The `frequency` JSON action establishes the loaded base with the same dynamic
chart as eigenmodes. It solves `(iωM-A) zhat=B` using the entire descriptor pencil,
retaining forced algebraic/DC response. Row/column equilibration, a reciprocal
condition estimate and original full-equation residuals accompany each frequency.
Singular/ill-conditioned frequencies remain explicit gaps; zero-frequency free
flight is commonly nonunique. Base trim controls are held at their solved values,
then selected flap/engine settings or gust channels provide unit harmonic inputs.

Complex Earth gusts combine streamwise phase with cosine/sine transverse span
families. The convection sign follows `ω=k·U_E`. Direction normalization and
transverse projection copy arrays rather than mutating the base orientation or
caller-owned vectors. Input columns sample the existing common gust field at
actual control/load/body/engine/point positions. Previous base gust fields are
superposed within the existing JSON evaluator's bounds. The maximum phase change
along an element is exported with a coarse-mesh flag, not an accuracy guarantee.

`output_perturbation` in the shared dynamic module evaluates state, time-derivative
and input perturbations together. That retains direct thrust/flap/gust loads,
rate lift and the strain-rate constitutive terms. The existing modal wrapper
continues to call the same output map without forcing. A shared `state_layout`
helper describes scales and coordinates. Operating-variable perturbations and
additional fluid-load components are now available alongside geometry, local
motion, section/strip outputs and the free-flight frame.

`web/frequency-results.js` supplies angular-frequency settings, input families,
Bode magnitude/dB and wrapped/unwrapped phase, physical output/station selection,
clickable sample markers, CSV and full JSON. Body/Earth phase playback uses
physical input amplitude rather than eigenvector shape normalization. Failed
frequencies display the base and an explicit unavailable message. Base metrics,
loading and Structure stay separate from the harmonic perturbation. Playback and
plot changes preserve saved results; input changes invalidate them. Browser
progress distinguishes linearization columns from completed frequencies.

`examples/forced-oscillator.asw` is an original ordinary-format spring–mass model
with a proportional Engine acting as a unit force actuator. Its exact tip
transfer is `1/[500(1+i*.02ω)-2ω²]`. No extra ASW record or point-load input extension
was introduced. `scripts/verify-frequency.py` records source-hashed resumable
mechanical and coupled heave/pitch/lag studies in
`docs/validation/frequency-response.json`. It uses 29 source hashes and six cases:
three oscillator tangent/mesh settings, then aspect ratios 40/80/160 for two
inputs (axis force per span and a uniform vertical gust) at five frequencies.

All six study cases passed. Maximum oscillator displacement error is
5.8761e-14 m per setting; maximum full-equation backward error is 2.0757e-17.
For the coupled model at 40 m/s, maximum response errors normalized separately

80 and 160. Both heave and pitch under both inputs approach the independent
five-state reference. Increasing span is not a mesh study at fixed aspect ratio;
this does not establish a converged finite-wing resonance or experimental parity.

## Scheduled feedback and integrated errors — 2026-10-04

`openswing/feedback.py` adds actual actuator settings as algebraic unknowns
and selected integrated measurement errors as differential states. The same
measurement evaluator drives time, modal and harmonic controller equations.
Multiple outputs can combine measurement-minus-command, integrated error and
raw-value terms, with scalar or bilinear true-airspeed/density gains. Acceleration
feedback stays inside the implicit residual; no prior-step measurement delay
or explicit feedback approximation is introduced.

Time startup first obtains the open-loop loaded base and default measurement
commands, then solves the structure/actuators with prescribed integral initial
conditions (zero by default). Modal/harmonic bases instead solve zero integral
derivatives. TimeState carries physical actuator/integral values and current
commands; frame slices are explicit because controller states follow the
frame. The continuous descriptor adds derivative columns only for integrals,
retains actual actuator columns algebraically, and exports their layout/scales.
Controller scaling uses aircraft dimensions rather than absolute Earth position.

`TimeForcing` accepts selected controller measurement names, including Sensor
suffixes and +initial-command offsets. The existing spline, multiplier/adder,
exact-knot and doubled-time behavior is retained. Controlled actuator Bode
inputs perturb the commanded setting; `command.NAME` adds a selected measurement
command. Gust inputs retain direct measurement feedthrough. Complex controller
reports contain actuator values, commands, measurements, errors and integrals.
Angle differences are wrapped in output derivatives, while control-law branch
crossings and nonunique scheduled-gain tangents are rejected.

`openswing/control_tables.py` parses original .con blocks, including gfac,
singleton grids, bilinear matrices and comments. Explicit input/output bindings
carry channel names, unit factors and extrapolation policy. The public manual
identifies global input j=6 (yaw rate), j=8 (pitch), and output 2 (elevator) in
examples. The linked WingLoop pitch example establishes j=5 (pitch rate) and
j=14 (pitch integral); do not confuse those internal indices with display-menu
indices in the guide. Complete INDEXC/KD maps and default actuator-unit
conventions remain unverified. The source text and bindings are retained in
exports; original files are not silently assigned guessed meanings.

`web/feedback-results.js` adds a controller editor, JSON/.con import, original
spring–mass PI preset, definition export, selected measurement Bode inputs and
physical/complex result table/CSV. Time histories and Bode plots expose actuator,
command, error and integral channels. The Controller tab follows the selected
time/mode/input/frequency, with explicit normalization independent of playback.
Sensor/controller tables now keep readable labels and units within their own
scroll region on narrow screens. `examples/position-controller.json` supplies
the original demo law for `instrumented-oscillator.asw`.

Twenty controller test cases cover independent PD/PI/acceleration-feedback
roots and transfers, direct gust-vane response, matrix-exponential time
refinement, constant-reference equilibrium, doubled-time command changes,
gain tables and malformed definitions, .con bindings, free-flight gain
derivatives, gain/angle branch guards and translated GPS origins. The 94 existing
time/forcing/modal/frequency/sensor regression cases passed. The six-case
`scripts/verify-feedback.py` study records original mechanical pole/transfer
and PI transient references, complete inputs and 31 generating-source hashes
in `docs/validation/feedback.json`. Final kernel/browser results follow below.
Earlier validation artifacts retain their historical hashes.

Remaining control work includes general dynamic/nonlinear custom routines,
complete default control-file maps and unit semantics, fully combined steady
operating/controller constraints, broader aircraft/rotating/gust feedback
validation and ASWING/experimental comparison. Broken-loop plots, initial-state
frequency forcing, root tracking/flutter boundaries, reduced models, remaining
gust/companion formats and the rest of the requirements ledger also remain.
The full goal remains active; this increment does not complete ASWING parity.

## Simultaneous steady controller and operating trim — 2026-10-04

`steady_feedback.py` adds the steady control-law equations to the existing
structural/circulation and operating equations. Actual actuator settings and
integrals are independent unknowns; every selected integrated error has zero
rate. Operating variables can include explicit measurement or actuator commands
(`command.RY[2]`, `command.F1`, `command.E1`). These commands have physical
scales and remain distinct from actual actuator settings in reports and exports.
Selecting an actuator already owned by feedback as an ordinary trim unknown is
rejected with the corresponding command name, rather than overwriting the law.

The seed solves the loaded structure at prescribed operating settings. Default
commands come from that seed, independently of whether an open-loop trim is
possible. The coupled solve continues operating targets with full physical
loads and controller gains. A full centered final tangent, normalized by column,
rejects redundant commands, integrals and trim targets even at zero residual.
This is a local rank diagnostic, not proof of uniqueness or stability. An
open-loop structural seed remains necessary. Initial integrals are steady
guesses; the time-startup interpretation remains prescribed initial conditions.

`solve_static` and the browser JSON bridge expose steady feedback. Modal and
harmonic analyses now solve the simultaneous closed-loop base before applying
their fixed/free-flight dynamic constraints. The trimmed commands become
constants; actual actuators and integrals remain dynamic state coordinates.
The original target and operating-variable reports are exported in
`base.steady_trim`. The browser offers command variables in the target editor,
steady Controller tables/CSV, and a separate base-trim report for dynamics.
Closed-loop static derivative requests are explicitly rejected pending a
complete coupled derivative implementation.

Twelve new native cases cover the analytical proportional spring response,
actuator/measurement command trim, PI integral equilibrium, retained modal/Bode
base and transfer, a controller that makes an open-loop singular speed-trim
target solvable, simultaneous aerodynamic lift/pitch trim, solved Earth pose,
redundant zero-residual PI constraints, actuator conflicts and JSON dispatch.
The additional elastic climbing-turn case solves all 16 trim equations with
four controlled actuators, comparing actual settings and deformed geometry to
an independently trimmed operating point. All 12 passed, as did the 20 existing
controller cases. The analytical speed and climbing-turn comparisons use a
1e-11 normalized solve tolerance: physical errors at the default tolerances
were consistent with force scaling but exceeded their stricter absolute test
thresholds.

`scripts/verify-control-trim.py` records spring command trim and released
spectra/transfers at 4/8 panels plus aerodynamic lift/pitch trim at 4/8/12
panels. Mechanical roots/transfers and zero section pitching moment are
independent references; the aerodynamic lift comparison uses the same kernel.
Final regression, study and browser results follow below. Older verification
artifacts retain their historical generating hashes.

Remaining control work includes general dynamic/nonlinear routines, complete
original index/unit maps, direct time initialization/restart from a saved trim,
closed-loop static derivatives and broader aircraft/experimental validation.
The full requirements ledger, including flutter tracking, ROMs, companion/gust
formats and complete ASWING numerical parity, remains active and incomplete.

## Custom nonlinear controller expressions and states — 2026-10-04

Outputs now choose scheduled terms, a complete target expression, or an
implicit scalar residual. Optional residual scales are explicit. Accessors read
current measurements, errors, built-in integrals, commands, actual actuator
settings, custom states and scalar/table parameters. Cross-actuator and
acceleration dependencies remain inside the common implicit residual. Bounded
arithmetic/math syntax is interpreted as a tree; no Python/Fortran code is
executed. Conditional branches and parameter lookup are lazy, including an
inactive branch whose gain table is outside its valid speed range.

Custom differential states follow actuator and built-in integral coordinates.
Users supply a scale, unit label, initial value and rate expression. Time startup
holds their initial values; steady/trim and modal/Bode bases solve zero rates.
State values and rates are exported in physical units, with modal/harmonic
values read directly from the solved descriptor coordinates. This avoids
cancellation noise when a steady harmonic state has exactly zero rate. The
browser includes an original actuator-lag preset, JSON examples for lag and
saturation/back-calculation anti-windup, state/rate tables, histories and
complex outputs/CSV, and command choices parsed from expression references.

Piecewise expressions and scheduled expression parameters activate one-sided
checks of complete controller residuals in the actual state, rate and harmonic
input directions. These reject incompatible local slopes, while accepting
smooth cancellations such as abs(error)^2. They remain numerical local checks;
rapid smooth variation can require a smaller difference step. Time-dependent
laws use the existing frozen-base modal/harmonic semantics.

The nonlinear saturation tests exposed stale-tangent iteration exhaustion in
the common modified Newton solver. It now refreshes after at most six accepted
corrections within a solve, or earlier when progress slows, and accepts a
converged final allowed correction. Tolerances and physical residual checks
are unchanged. The affected lag/anti-windup checks pass after this correction.

The custom native suite covers lag roots/transfers and matrix-exponential time
refinement, built-in integrals inside expressions, nonlinear implicit outputs,
cross-coupled actuators, saturated anti-windup equilibrium/spectra/transfer,
independent piecewise ODE time refinement, scheduled gain derivatives,
state/rate/input switching tangents, smooth composites, lazy branches and
definition/syntax/domain failures. `scripts/verify-custom-control.py` records
the independent original mechanical references and their generating hashes.
Final native, study, build, browser and archive checks follow below.

The interface supports named signals and custom scalar differential states;
it is not arbitrary legacy procedural CONTROL compatibility and does not expose
all internal ASWING arrays. Original index/unit maps, saved trim/time restart,
closed-loop static derivatives, broader aircraft/experimental validation and
the remaining full requirements ledger are still incomplete. The goal remains
active; this increment does not claim full ASWING parity.

## Selected-mode reduced-order models (2026-10-04)

The previous goal turn made concrete progress on nonlinear controller/state
laws. This increment implements the previously missing selected-mode ROM
path documented in unsteady theory §13.3.4. `openswing/reduced_model.py` and the
`rom` JSON action compute real A/B/C/D matrices, derivative-input sensor
feedthrough, right state maps and a mass-dual state projection. Any returned
modes may be selected; complex conjugates are completed automatically. The
selected mass Gram matrix is normalized as a group, including repeated
semisimple poles. Dependent/defective selections and failed full-equation
invariance/pairing checks are explicit errors.

A separate algebraic input lift uses the *full* finite subspace and the mass
null space. This recovers direct reaction and acceleration response missing
from homogeneous modes, even in a truncated ROM. Its rank, consistency and
zero-mass checks reject inputs requiring unsupported descriptor-state input
derivatives. Physical global/Sensor output directions include both state and
rate effects. Declared settings, feedback commands and fixed spatial gust
families are supported; frequency-dependent convected-gust matrices remain.

`web/rom-results.js` adds a panel inside Eigenmodes. It reuses the immutable
saved modal request, offers mode/input selection and named sensor/global
outputs, compares reduced/full complex response on a requested frequency grid,
plots magnitude, and exports JSON plus real matrix text. Controller command
inputs are listed from the active signal map. ROM edits invalidate its exports;
phase animation does not mutate matrices or the underlying modal result.
Complete base/state-layout metadata is in JSON. The plain text is an original
OpenSwing format, not a claimed legacy .rom writer. The public manuals describe its contents but not its exact layout. An initial
read-only tree inspection of the Leonardo Avoni companion repository found no
ROM-named artifact. A subsequent inspection of the separate ISAE experimental
validation repository found published .rom examples, recorded below for the
next compatibility work.

## Annotated ROM files and independent viewer (2026-10-04)

This increment implements the interchange step identified above.
`openswing/rom_file.py` parses the observed annotated eigenvalue/eigenvector,
input-row, output-column and final direct-matrix sections. It preserves exact
original text separately from normalized serialization, accepts Fortran D and
compact exponents, and validates complete matching indices/channels/units.
Unknown labels remain opaque; absent physical input units are not inferred.
Realization and harmonic evaluation reconcile known differences between
eigenvalue and B-coefficient time units while retaining raw printed matrices.
Complex representatives include their conjugates; real poles contribute once.
Ambiguous double signs, inconsistent real-pole phases, complex direct terms
and incomplete files are explicit errors. Retained poles create response gaps.

The `rom_import` JSON action needs only text and frequencies. `web/rom-file.js`
adds an independent ROM files tab with real matrices, literal modal values,
magnitude/phase plots and response tables, original/normalized downloads and
JSON export. It keeps imported data independent of the current aircraft and
invalidates responses after frequency edits. Mobile tables scroll within their
containers. The generated-ROM panel offers annotated `.rom` export when its
modal blocks and sensor feedthrough fit the layout. Time and dimensional
measurements use SI, angular measurements use degrees, physical command/gust
inputs use SI, and flap/engine inputs keep their original setting units.
Custom command/gust/global Earth-velocity labels are explicit extensions.
Material derivative-input feedthrough disables only this export; JSON/text
retain the full model, including baseline and state maps.
