## Operating-point stability progression (2026-10-04)

The preceding ROM exchange increment was progress. This increment adds the
MODE operating-point progression workflow described by the public user guide.
`openswing/stability.py` and the `stability` bridge action solve independent
loaded equilibria and frozen full-residual eigenmodes over a prescribed grid.
Parameters include speed, alpha/beta, atmospheric altitude/density, declared
actuators and explicit zero-based operating-target entries. Trim unknowns
cannot simultaneously be prescribed sweep variables. Feedback remains in
speed/target sweeps; ambiguous actuator-command semantics are rejected.

Tracking compares right vectors after undoing changing solver scales in one
fixed physical-coordinate metric. It collapses conjugate signs without merging
independent repeated pairs, uses shape assurance and secant root prediction,
and computes a one-to-one assignment with optional unmatched roots. The
initial separate row/column ambiguity check was too restrictive for the
nonnormal heave/pitch modes; the final check compares the complete assignment
with an alternative that forbids the proposed pair. Ambiguous, missing,
real/complex-splitting and failed roots create explicit gaps. The implementation
does not infer an instability bracket across a gap.

Sign-changing branches support safeguarded secant refinement with matching to
both endpoints. Both a narrow parameter bracket and small normalized growth
are required for a resolved boundary. The reported value is an actually
computed point inside the final bracket. Discontinuous sign jumps, failed
refinement solves and iteration exhaustion remain unresolved. Oscillatory
candidates, aperiodic crossings and stabilizing transitions are distinguished;
none is automatically identified as structural flutter.

`web/stability-results.js` adds the sweep controls, root/growth plots, full
finite-spectrum coverage, points with growing roots, ambiguity/error messages,
JSON/path CSV and computed-point selection. The selected point can use existing
mode playback, physical output and ROM workflows. Saved sweep data do not
change during phase playback; edited aircraft or sweep inputs invalidate the
relevant exports. The browser worker reports point/linearization progress and
existing cancellation terminates its computation. Source/runtime stay local.

new JSON-bridge actuator/target sweep cases in 32.19 s. The latter recover the
independent spring displacement setting/500 at each loaded point. The first

on a model with additional relaxation roots; the corrected test explicitly

was not rerun. Logs are `/tmp/openswing-stability-native-final.log`,

## Physical equilibrium continuation and adaptive tracking (2026-10-04)

The previous stability increment was progress. This increment adds a physical
steady-equilibrium seed across mounted/constrained solves, modal and harmonic
bases, selected-mode ROM generation and stability sweeps. These are OpenSwing
version-1 JSON packets, explicitly distinct from ASWING `.pnt`/`.set` and from
unsteady restart. Exact source/mesh compatibility is required. Numerical solver
scales are recomputed for each requested condition; the packet preserves
positions, rotation vectors, internal forces/moments, reaction types and
circulation in physical input units. Selected trim guesses are re-encoded from
physical operating values. Every seed reuse solves the complete loaded residual
and checks the final tangent; no unloaded fallback is hidden from the user.

Controller packets include actual actuators, integrated errors, custom states,
layout/order/units, solved commands and original prescribed biases. Same-layout
controllers can change coefficients/equations. Unspecified commands retain solved
values; explicit commands and changed prescribed biases override them. Command
trim, actuator equilibrium and zero state rates are solved together. The seed
is captured before dynamic analyses release steady operating constraints.

The browser Saved equilibrium panel saves/imports JSON, accepts complete results
containing a seed, exposes an explicit start checkbox and rejects incompatible
meshes. Inputs preserve the loaded seed while invalidating the latest result.
Mode phase playback leaves exports unchanged. Time response does not use these
packets. ROM builds initialize from the selected computed modal base.

Warm sweeps initialize from their original modal base, then the nearest solved
lower-parameter point. Optional bounded midpoint subdivision responds to a
failed corrector or uncertain assignment. Warm right endpoints are recomputed
after intermediate solves. Prior attempts remain in JSON with `superseded_by`;
only final attempts enter convergence/coverage and the browser point selector.
The tracked sequence is recorded separately. Budget exhaustion and unresolved
assignments remain explicit gaps. Exact assignment ties cannot be accepted by
setting the ambiguity margin to zero. Local warm correction does not establish
branch uniqueness or follow a fold; search-window/subspace handling remains open.

## Physical time checkpoints and continuation (2026-10-04)

The previous saved-equilibrium/adaptive-tracking turn made verified progress.
The current increment implements continuation from a computed time state, as
required by the public guide's append/target-point time workflow. It does not
claim complete companion-file parity or direct launch from saved steady trim.

`time_state.py` stores physical elastic velocities/rates, nodal rotations,
resultants/reactions, circulation, frame motion/pose and controller states. The
BDF predecessor, proposed next step and original relative-forcing offsets are
retained. Setup includes the load-attachment union so release does not change
the mesh or solver normalization. Controller defaults and numerical scales are
restored without binding commands to a new measured value. `resume_time` checks
source/mesh/layout, finite arrays, proper frame orientation and the instantaneous
physical/algebraic residual; it does not solve a new equilibrium. The LU tangent
is rebuilt. Results expose absolute start/end times and per-snapshot restart data.

`solve_time` and `resume_time` share the integration loop. Replaced forcing text
is an explicit input change: the old state is retained, BDF history is discarded,
and the new table must cover the new interval. Relative offsets remain tied to
the original trajectory. A checkpoint at a doubled-time event keeps left-hand
state and resumes first-order with right-hand forcing. Altered maximum steps
respect the saved proposal and existing 1.5 growth limit.

The browser can save/use a selected snapshot or load standalone checkpoints/full
time results. Continuing a selected state keeps its prefix and replaces its
future; imported checkpoints create a new segment. Prefix snapshots retain
original contexts when the future table/settings change. Plot axes and playback
use absolute start/end times, and plot discontinuities retain earlier breaks.
Source/setup/control edits are separate from continuation settings. Old exports
remain immutable, including through failed imports/resumes.

## Mixed continuous dynamics and harmonic frame inputs (2026-10-04)

The preceding goal turn made verified progress on mixed time constraints and
finite forcing tables. This increment extends the shared continuous dynamic
chart to fixed/prescribed/free/mixed layouts. `make_system` constructs per-axis net-load
constraints from `load_targets`, uses them for the base when no separate trim is
supplied, and requires the converged base to satisfy the selected dynamic rows.
Prescribed, mixed and free motion retain all twelve frame kinematic states, including the
Euler chart, base trajectory derivative and reference transport. Fixed frame
continues to omit those coordinates. Invalid layouts fail before solving.

`HarmonicInput` now accepts active `target.force.x/y/z` and
`target.moment.x/y/z`, or prescribed `acceleration.x/y/z` and
`angular_acceleration.x/y/z`. It rejects conflicting/inactive columns and fixed
frame use. Actual motion and condition overrides are consistent, so physical
balance, kinematics, sensors and direct output share the input. Units are input
F, F L, L/T² and rad/T²; the latter differs from ASW time-table G columns. Existing
controller commands retain their own path. Mixed-frame tangent checks include
speed scheduling. Result/base metadata preserves the constant target map.

The browser has per-axis selectors for both modes and Bode, a six-channel frame
input option, stale-result invalidation, physical-unit plots and CSV. ROM input
selection includes the frame channels. The shared reduced-model API retains the
same layout, and annotated `.rom` export converts rad/T² to rad/s² while marking
custom frame labels as extensions. General inverse constraints remain required.

Native focused checks passed **12 cases in 90.77 s**, followed by **two offset
reference cases in 30.58 s**, **two controller/ROM cases in 27.32 s**, and **one
SI-conversion case in 1.87 s**. The offset reference is an independent twelve-state
Newton–Euler ODE with nonzero rotation, nonzero targets and three separate ASW
reference points; complex-step ODE derivatives are compared with the full
constrained beam pencil at two differentiation steps. Other tests verify all six

## Exact coordinate-integrator modes (2026-10-04)

The preceding rotating-body study exposed a native/WASM sensitivity: defective
zero roots split into approximately 1e-5/s apparent growth/decay despite tiny
pencil backward errors. `IntegratorDeflation` now applies exact row/column
Laplace expansion before the descriptor constraint staircase. A zero A column
with exactly one nonzero M entry factors out one lambda, as does its row
analogue. Repetition handles coordinate chains. No entry tolerance or small-root
snapping is used. The remaining finite modes use the existing dense or
shift-and-invert solve, and nonzero vectors are lifted by reverse substitution.

Zero vectors come from the original A and transpose kernels, with complete
pivoting that retains weak nonzero pivots. All pairs still satisfy the original
full pencil. Algebraic multiplicity is retained; repeated vectors for a
defective pole do not form a Jordan basis. Independent semisimple zeros retain
a checked mass-dual ROM basis; defective selections and underdetermined
algebraic freedom remain rejected. The all-zero A diagnostic now avoids 0/0,
and an empty finite quotient reports a null mass condition number.

Mode JSON/CSV exposes `exact_integrator` and `stability_tolerance`. The UI names
certified integrator zeros and shows their count. Nonzero roots inside the growth
display threshold are labeled near neutral, with their computed values retained
and the threshold explicitly distinguished from an eigenvalue error bound.
The operation report includes original row/column indices, pivot, retained
indices, original-kernel dimension estimate and finite quotient dimension.

## Matched broken-loop Bode display (2026-10-05)

The ASWING guide and unsteady formulation §13.2 explicitly define an alternative
Bode display `1-u/x`, meaningful for a response x corresponding to command u.
`frequency_response.py` now records that scalar ratio alongside each physical
harmonic solution. Command/response matching is explicit metadata, with the same
physical units on both sides. Actual flap/engine operating settings include
implicit controller and actuator-state effects; measurement commands use their
matching measured values. Active frame-load targets use actual net force/moment
components, and prescribed accelerations use their corresponding operating
values. Gust fields have no unique matching aircraft state for this definition.

The transform uses a scaled complex reciprocal, with `(H-1)/H` near H=1 to avoid
avoidable cancellation. There is no small-response snapping. Exact zero H and
overflow produce explicit unavailable records; a zero transformed value retains
zero magnitude and undefined dB/phase. Physical solve convergence is independent
of display availability. `broken_loop_output` identifies the matched physical
quantity; `broken_loop` contains H, the transformed value, or an explicit error.

The browser Display selector switches between physical x/u and broken-loop
1-u/x. It automatically uses the matching response and hides unrelated output
choices. Gain/phase plots and CSV carry the chosen definition and units, preserve
frequency gaps and restart phase unwrapping after undefined data. The physical
response, arbitrary output selections, geometry/playback and exported JSON are
unchanged by display choices. The scalar ratio retains the other loops' solved
configuration; it is not a general multivariable loop-removal or margin algorithm.
Small nonzero H can amplify numerical errors, so source/full-equation residuals
are not advertised as forward error bounds for this plot.

Validation completed before the source-hashed study:

- **18 focused tests passed** in 42.37 s, followed by **one input-time-unit test**
  in 11.62 s. Independent mechanical equations check PD/PI, acceleration feedback,
  actuator lag and two coupled implicit actuators. Other checks cover unsupported
  gust pairing, a truly unresponsive command, six mixed frame input mappings,
  physical DC gaps, and high-precision extreme/near-unit complex ratios. The first
  focused run exposed controller settings in the wrong level of the new test's
  JSON request; the fixture was corrected before the passing run.
- **41 regression tests passed** in 307.49 s: existing full-descriptor Bode,
  complex gust and direct-feedthrough physics, frame constraints, closed-loop
  poles/transfers and implicit actuator-state/cross-coupling cases.
- **Six browser tests passed** in 4.0 minutes, terminal exit 0, using the packaged
  WebAssembly app. The two new offline scenarios check actual-engine and
  measurement command transforms, undefined command/gust gaps, CSV formula and
  units, phase/view changes, immutable JSON and desktop/mobile layout. Existing
  physical oscillator response, geometry, gust family and free-flight DC-gap
  scenarios also passed. Desktop/mobile broken-loop screenshots were inspected;
  there were no page errors or horizontal overflow in the new main scenario.

The independent spring-mass plant has `P=2s²+10s+500`. With feedback C, the actual
actuator's display is `-C/P`; including command-before-actuator lag changes it to
`-tau*s-C/P`. Position-command tracking has a different numerator and a different
ratio. These checks detect an incorrect sign, reciprocal, matching channel,
injection location, missing direct output or dropped cross-coupling.

Review found that accepted leading-zero actuator indices (for example
`power.01`) needed canonical matching to the actual `power.1` output. That
metadata lookup is now normalized through the parsed index. The final focused

invariance. The PD study case uses the alias so the packaged WASM comparison
also exercises it. The first WASM attempt was intentionally interrupted after
its first case while this fix was made; it was not counted as a complete pass.

## Published flying-wing comparison and descriptor robustness (2026-10-05)

This increment uses the separately fetched MIT `fw.asw` and `root_map_fw.pdf`.
The reference extractor pins the PDF hash, checks its vector-path layout,
extracts 108 plotted marker centers and records the visually transcribed twelve
trim rows. The public figure's setup does not specify its mesh, interpolation,
Mach setting or executable version. The glide constraints are inferred from
its elevation, alpha and drag/lift values. This is partial published validation;
exact discrete/executable parity and experimental validation remain open.

The first sideslip tangent exposed a force-point self-vortex cancellation bug:
subtracting separately evaluated near-singular bound velocities left a false
velocity large enough to trip the subsonic guard. Physical self-bound segments
are now omitted before wake summation; their complete ground images remain.
Independent wake/image line integrals and near-filament load continuity verify
the fix. The original Mach guard remains in place.

The numerical constraint staircase also discarded resolved weak inertias at
the default rank cutoff and returned only three coordinate zeros for this
case. Its initial guard now rejects resolved discarded singular values even
when they are more than two decades below the requested cutoff. The added
`full_shift_invert` method applies complex Arnoldi to the shifted original
pencil after exact integrator factorization. It retains weak inertia and
algebraic equations, checks full left/right equations, and explicitly leaves
the total finite dimension unclassified. It does not make a completeness claim
or bypass the ROM's separate algebraic-input-lift check.

## 2026-10-05 — Independent Fourier circulation coordinates

Implemented the steady theory's equations 63, 150–151 and 201 as a reduced
circulation space. Each logical lifting beam can select K sine
modes or retain pointwise circulation. The material Glauert angles remain fixed
under deformation. Physical horseshoes and loads retain all P structural
intervals; the complete local flow equation is tested against the sine basis.
The common residual carries these coordinates through static, time, controller,
derivative, eigenmode, harmonic and reduced-model calculations. Invalid counts,
unknown/nonlifting beams and ill-conditioned sampling are rejected.

Saved equilibria and time checkpoints still contain physical circulation on
every interval. Mode counts bind their identity, and restored states must lie
in the selected space. Default pointwise identities remain compatible.
Descriptor state layouts identify the coefficient block. Browser per-beam
controls, exports and solver reports expose the representation, coefficients,
weighted residual and separate local flow defect. The latter can remain nonzero
after the weighted equations converge; it is displayed with a refinement note.

`docs/validation/circulation.json` pins 45 inputs: all 40 kernel modules, the
verification script, the published reference transcription, the previous
Trefftz study, and the two original example inputs. It includes three elliptic
panel checks, five rectangular mode checks, three coupled spectra and six
flying-wing trims. The Fourier trims start cold; previous pointwise states are
used only for matching pointwise warm solves. No physical constants are fitted.

## 2026-10-05 — Closed-loop quasi-steady derivatives

Removed the former rejection of derivative requests with steady feedback.
`derivatives.py` now includes actual actuators, integrated errors and custom
controller states in the equilibrium tangent. It uses the common network and
measurement/control residual with zero local and controller rates, following
steady equations 212–213 and unsteady equations 117–122. The structural,
circulation and optional six-acceleration responses retain their existing
physical scaling, output axes and fixed coefficient normalization.

Original trim targets are released. Their solved commands remain fixed except
the selected command input, without reinitializing default measurements or
holding integrals at their seed values. Controlled actuators use explicit
`command.F#`/`command.E#` columns; selected measurement commands are also
available. Uncontrolled inputs retain their previous names. Actuator/measurement/
integral/custom-state output matrices carry physical row units. Controller
commands in angular channels use degrees while the flight alpha/beta columns
retain radians. A copied network and command maps preserve the solved base.
One-sided composite-residual guards, angle branches, schedule slope checks and
the complete tangent rank test reject nonunique or nonsmooth derivatives.

The browser updates available derivative inputs when feedback changes and
preserves an actuator selection when it becomes a command selection. It exposes
**Controller & measurements**, full JSON and CSV, closed-loop interpretation
and the usual structural derivative plots. Disabling feedback restores the
uncontrolled input and invalidates the old results.

## 2026-10-05 — Editable material node distributions

The previous increment made verified progress on closed-loop steady derivatives.
This increment implements per-logical-beam node controls described by the NODE
menu, while retaining the open requirements for separate aerodynamic/structural
sampling meshes and exact ASWING grid/zero-length-interval behavior.

`openswing/discretization.py` accepts an integer cosine count or normalized
`panels` settings with a global default and per-beam cosine/uniform counts or
explicit `t` nodes. Counts mean intervals before inserting mandatory stations.
Generated spacing uses undeformed material arc length; explicit lists include
both logical-domain endpoints and are never implicitly mirrored. Strict checks
reject invalid counts, missing beams, mixed forms, unordered/nonfinite nodes,
incorrect endpoints and near-coincident intervals. Settings do not modify ASW
property distributions or source text. This is an OpenSwing setting, not a
new ASW property or guessed legacy `.set` format.

The same required-node collection now serves inspection, rigid aerodynamics and
structural networks. Endpoints, mirrored/property breaks, joints, grounds,
weights, engines, sensors, struts and applied loads are retained. This corrects
an earlier preview/rigid versus structural discrepancy at interior attachments;
rigid results on those configurations can change with the added intervals.
The static JSON boundary now forwards applied nodal loads, matching the native
API and inspection. Rigid position jumps still contain no beam material and
retain conservative force/moment transfer. Material Glauert angles and actual
interval quadrature weights drive the existing Fourier equations on these
nonuniform grids.

The **Beam nodes** browser tab edits counts or explicit stations, displays a
required-node table, and plots nodes plus first/highest Fourier basis waves
against material arc fraction or angle. Invalid drafts leave the applied mesh
and current result intact; successful changes invalidate results. Property
editing preserves mesh choices and validates them against its new geometry;
opening a new ASW document clears beam overrides. Mesh JSON import/export,
result requests, steady launch settings and BDF checkpoints retain the chosen
mesh. Saved-state identity checks reject changed actual nodes. Steady JSON
exports now include the complete analysis request, as dynamic exports already
did. Desktop and 390-pixel mobile layouts were visually inspected.

## 2026-10-05 — Consistent initial disturbances in frequency response

The full objective remains **active and incomplete**. This increment adds
physical initial-state profiles to the local frequency-response workflow. The
public ASWING homepage lists initial-condition frequency response; the unsteady
formulation §§13.3.3–13.3.4 supplies the homogeneous descriptor dynamics and
rate-dependent output map. Applying the one-sided Laplace transform gives
`(s M-A) X=M x0` and `Y=C X+Q(s X-x0)`. This implementation uses that full system,
including initial-value terms in damping, apparent mass, accelerometers and
controller state-rate outputs. It does not infer a legacy serialized format.

The new `openswing/initial_response.py` is the 42nd packaged kernel module.
Physical profiles support exact material nodes or linear tables in arbitrary t,
body-axis displacement/spatial rotation/elastic velocity/rates, physical panel
circulation, moving-frame velocity/rates/Earth pose and controller integrals or
custom states. All are increments from the loaded base; omissions are zero.
Tables require exact domain endpoints, and exact-node matching respects tiny
parameter scales. The Fourier basis performs its existing circulation encoding
check. Duplicate fields, unsupported fields, complex/nonfinite values and
incompatible dynamic constraints are rejected.

The complete finite constraint subspace completes resultants, reactions,
accelerations and actuator increments. It retains constitutive relaxation and
integrator/Jordan chains without selected-mode projection. Input consistency is
checked relative to profile amplitude, so tiny incompatible inputs cannot evade
rejection. The completed state/rate, physical initial output, rank history,
full-equation residuals and finite spectrum are exported. The existing weak
inertia guard and full-pencil conditioning checks remain in force.

A nonnegative Laplace damping σ must exceed the complete resolved spectral
abscissa plus the reported numerical margin. σ=0 is available for decaying
systems. Free flight, neutral or unstable systems require a positive value;
this condition is conservative even for a profile that might avoid a growing
mode. It is subject to rank, scaling, mesh and tangent refinement. Periodic
inputs remain at σ=0 and are factored separately when needed. A periodic DC
pole can therefore remain a gap while the initial spectrum is available at the
same frequency. Counts, plots and diagnostics now retain per-input availability.

The browser adds physical-profile editing/import/export, initial-only or mixed
input selection, Laplace damping and rank settings, spectral units and CSV.
Phase animation is hidden for initial spectra and geometry shows the loaded
base. The final visual review replaced a misleading generic harmonic caption
with the initial-spectrum interpretation and generalized the frequency-mode
labels. `examples/initial-spring.json` contains original displacement and
velocity releases for the instrumented oscillator. README, numerical notes and
the requirement ledger describe schema, equations, convergence, units and limits.
Two older README passages were also corrected to acknowledge the already
implemented direct launch from saved steady trim.

## 2026-10-05 — Physical derivative coefficients for loaded aircraft

The preceding initial-spectrum increment was verified progress. The full goal
remains **active and incomplete**. This increment addresses its unresolved
swept/twisted aircraft derivative-rank failure directly, rather than accepting
a smaller spectrum or weakening the inertia guard.

A source-level review and finite-rate probes identified cancellation in the
old mass-matrix stencil. At fixed state, local acceleration/angular-acceleration
loads are linear, while circulation-rate tangency drag is quadratic. For the
original `flexible.asw` at 30 m/s, alpha 4 degrees, zero gravity, 4 intervals and
3 Fourier modes, centered full-residual differences at step 1e-5 left a discarded
derivative singular value near 9.9183e-14. It fell to roughly 1e-18 with finite
symmetric coefficient probes, while the retained weak physical singular values
remained around 5.5e-7 and above. The complete finite spectrum then resolved
35 states. The original guard was correctly detecting an ambiguous numerical
matrix; it has not been relaxed.

`openswing/descriptor_mass.py`, the 43rd kernel module, now constructs the
continuous derivative matrix from the shared physical load evaluator. Symmetric
probes at plus/minus V/L extract the linear coefficient before adding loaded
internal forces and support reactions. Exact kinematic blocks retain their
original signs, reference points and input-time units. Dynamic net-load rows
use the same differentiated nodal wrenches. Jangle rows use the local spline
slope and the SO(3) logarithm derivative, including end-trace signs and offsets.
Smooth controller rows compose physical measurement derivatives with local
fourth-order scalar derivatives. Piecewise expressions retain differences and
one-sided checks on the complete physical path; this preserves smooth
cancellations between coincident sensors and checks quadratically reached
switches. Ordinary time/static controller evaluation delegates to the same
measurement-algebra method. No matrix entry or root is snapped to zero.

Modal, Bode/initial and ROM diagnostics identify the derivative construction.
The same continuous tangent is used by stability sweeps. The state/input
finite-difference stencils, underlying nonlinear loads and physical inertia
models are unchanged. Rank, full-equation residual and conditioning guards
remain active, including the synthetic true-weak-inertia rejection test.

The first packaged comparison exposed a separate cancellation in physical
output recovery for small initial-spectrum directions: a 3e-6 stencil times a
tiny spectrum gave section-load differences up to 1.5158245e-7 between native
and WASM. Homogeneous output directions now enlarge their stencil using both
state and rate scales, retaining the original state stencil for ordinary
normalized modes. Physical forcing retains its input-amplitude cap. The first
attempt also shrank ordinary modal increments by their rate scale, which
failed an existing strict constitutive-load test through position-subtraction
roundoff. Preserving the established mode stencil corrected it; that test and
an additional 1e-12-amplitude load-homogeneity check passed together in 15.36 s.
The cross-platform comparison tolerance was not loosened. A later pointwise-
circulation comparison exposed a study-fixture phase ambiguity: tied symmetric
tip components selected opposite eigenvector pivots on native and WASM. The
resulting initial disturbances were opposites; their physical loads agreed to
2.3e-12 after sign alignment. The study now records an explicit coordinate phase
anchor and reuses it in WASM, also checking the aligned complex mode itself.
This changes the verification fixture, not the solver's valid mode normalization.

## 2026-10-05 — Nonlinear physical initial disturbances and Radau integration

The full ASWING objective remains **active and incomplete**. This increment adds
compatible physical disturbances to saved-equilibrium nonlinear time launch and
three-stage Radau IIA integration for constrained motion.

`nonlinear_initial.py` holds prescribed dynamic profile coordinates fixed and
completes algebraic state and physical rates using the common residual and its
first two time derivatives. Finite SO(3) nodal/frame charts support the Euler
display pole. Cubic Taylor jets, sixth-order centered stencils, rank-aware
Gauss–Newton iterations, independent required-variable nullspace checks,
one-sided derivatives and half-spacing completion provide local numerical
evidence. They do not establish general higher-index/nonsmooth regularity.

The full pendulum trajectory exposed a separate BDF startup limitation: despite
an independently correct initial state, its peak reaction/acceleration transient
did not shrink on time-step refinement. `radau_time.py`, the 46th kernel module,
adds three-stage Radau IIA (`order=5`). Each stage satisfies the continuous
physical equations, without mass inversion, constraint projection or artificial
damping. ODE order five does not imply fifth-order constrained velocities or
reactions. BDF behavior is retained and its startup limitation is documented.
The last Radau stage receives the exact event time, preventing subtraction and
readdition roundoff from moving it across a forcing discontinuity.

The browser adds a physical-state JSON editor, single-profile import/export,
spacing/rank controls, progress and Radau launch/continuation choices. The same
profile schema serves linear initial response and ROMs. New time forcing starts
after the initialized snapshot. Saved-base consistency and topology requirements
remain; arbitrary cold/support-release construction is not claimed.

  in 314.86 s, followed by the gust/empirical-lag check in 86.93 s. Coverage
  includes initializer compatibility, units/scaling, unresolved physical rates,
  opposed one-sided acceleration constraints, nonfinite samples, high-index
  pendulum convergence, stiff-ODE response, forcing jumps/cutoff, checkpoint
  continuation and the existing BDF regressions. The gust check separates
  temporal refinement from finite-span error against its infinite-span reference.

  .0337742 for the integral/lag controller, .2485014 for the pendulum, and
  .0316711 for the torque-free body at 90-degree pitch.
- The pendulum's maximum y-support-force error decreases from .00626465 to

## 2026-10-05 — gust-aware reference-airflow operating constraints

Previous turn classification: **verified progress**. The full ASWING objective
remains active and incomplete. This increment addresses the reference velocity
constraints in the public steady formulation, equations 181–184, which include
the gust at the velocity reference. Existing direct speed/angle and unprefixed
EAS/pressure targets described still-atmosphere motion and could not impose
these local air-data targets in a gust.

- Added the 50th kernel module, `reference_flow.py`. It samples the Earth gust
  at the posed body-fixed velocity reference and adds it to the still-air
  reference vector. Rotation is already included in the existing velocity
  parameterization and is not counted twice. Induced/local elastic flow is
  excluded according to the documented reference definition.
- Added `reference.speed`, `reference.alpha`, `reference.beta`,
  `reference.equivalent_airspeed` and `reference.dynamic_pressure` to the common
  coupled residual. Alpha uses wrapped error and shortest continuation across
  ±180 degrees. Undefined angles remain null; active singular angle targets,
  invalid ranges and nonpositive speed/pressure targets fail explicitly.

## 2026-10-05 — weighted trim for redundant flap and engine controls

Previous turn classification: **verified progress**. The active full-scope goal
is unchanged. ASWING v5.86 documents a least-squares constraint option for
redundant controls and individual flap/engine weights. No exact weight formula
is published there. OpenSwing now provides the capability with an explicit
objective, while exact ASWING weighting and nonlinear branch parity remain open.

- Added the 51st kernel module, `control_allocation.py`. The objective is
  `J = 1/2 sum(weight * (setting - preferred)^2)` over all solved flap/engine
  variables. Positive weights and preferred settings are carried on operating
  rows. `minimum_control` slots add redundant actuator unknowns; all physical
  and other operating equations remain hard equalities.
- The coupled optimization uses a loaded prescribed-control equilibrium or
  saved physical state, continuation of hard targets, weighted actuator
  coordinates, exact objective gradients and centered physical derivatives.
  It retains the full structural, lifting-line, propulsion, inertia and
  controller equations rather than allocating loads against a frozen gain map.
- Final checks require physical residual tolerance, full equality-row rank,
  feasible-direction stationarity and positive reduced Lagrangian curvature.
  The curvature includes nonlinear physical-equation terms and uses analytic
  objective terms to avoid large-cost cancellation. Feasible directions are
  normalized by weighted actuator motion. This is a checked local minimum,
  not a proof of global optimality, aircraft stability or uniqueness of branches.
- Controller-owned actuators are excluded from this selected-actuator objective
  and retain their controller equations. Other redundant actuators can be
  allocated in the same solve. Bounds and saturation are not imposed. Invalid
  weights, non-actuator minimum slots, duplicate hard targets and nonzero
  physical targets on minimum slots fail explicitly.
- The browser exposes least-squares slots, a shared weight/preferred-setting
  editor for every solved actuator, and an optimization report. Cost changes
  invalidate results. Minimum rows do not display a false hard target. The
  original `redundant-thrust.asw` example supplies analytical force/moment and
  weighted allocation references without external input files.
- Saved equilibria preserve solved controls and cost metadata. Steady targets
  are released in modal, frequency, derivative and time-launch responses.
  The saved redundant spring checks retain the exact physical equilibrium and
  analytical transfer from each independent engine input.

The native study has seven cases: weighted proportional thrust, simultaneous
force/moment with nonzero preferred settings, a controller-owned engine,
nonlinear actuator disks with an independently thrust-parameterized optimum,
elastic proportional flaps, saved spring/frequency response, and millisecond
units with common weight scaling. It checks 40 scalar reference values and

weighted-projection reference; this does not independently validate the full
wing deformation. Current-source native/WASM evidence is recorded in
`docs/validation/control-allocation*.json`. Prior reference-flow, frequency and
body studies retain their historical kernel hashes after this increment.

## 2026-10-06 elastic rotor-mount whirl validation

Added original `examples/whirl-flutter.asw` and its example-menu entry, independent
`scripts/verify-whirl.py`, packaged replay `scripts/test-whirl-wasm.mjs`, and two
offline workflows in `tests/browser/whirl.spec.js`. The kernel's Engine type 2
mount-rate loads, point-object angular-momentum transport and coupled structural
modal/Bode/stability solves are exercised together. No numerical-kernel source
changed. This is a verified application and evidence increment, not a new rotor
force law or a claim of complete ASWING parity.

The original massless one-metre beam has equal EI=5 N m², a clamped root, pinned
tip translation, finite EA=1000 N and rigid shear/torsion. Finite EA is necessary:
the exploratory perfectly inextensible straight beam had redundant axial
support reactions and was correctly rejected. The tip carries transverse
inertia .2 kg m² and spin Hx=-1.8 kg m²/s. Engine 1 is an ideal zero-thrust
rotor with fixed design-inflow integrals and disabled jet; engines 2/3 apply
unit y/z test couples. Moments are measured about the fixed tip pin.

The independent reference condenses beam flexibility into
`k_N=(EI/L)(4N²-1)/(N²-1)`, with continuum limit `4EI/L`, and forms the two-axis
gyroscopic equations. It compares all four finite roots, forbidden motions,
physical mode polarization and both direct/cross-axis torque responses. Direct
azimuthal blade-force integration checks the moment derivatives for both spin
directions, with maximum absolute error **1.0230316593862199e-11** in SI units.
The tested speed sweep holds the input's blade integrals fixed; its boundary is
for that documented approximation, not a blade-resolved or experimental rotor.

0.0020793888567010315**. The computed four-interval crossing is

## 2026-10-06 derived section loads and elastic incidence

The preceding goal turn made verified progress by completing the airflow
increment and its bundle audit. This turn implements four explicitly documented
section outputs: local quarter-chord cm, f_aero, f_reac and da_eff. They are
available in steady and time results, browser loading plots, sampled histories,
envelopes, saved archives and CSV. Plot notes and exported metadata identify
the force components, current-length normalization, material sampling and units.
Missing historical fields and body-only samples remain gaps.

f_aero contains circulatory and enabled circulation-rate lift, projected on the
physical section normal; profile and apparent-mass forces remain separate.
f_reac combines distributed ordinary/additional mass gravity/inertia with
apparent force, excluding concentrated masses, supports and other point loads.
Network results use the existing moving-mass quadrature and preserve result
ownership when gravity changes while the aerodynamic cache is reused. The
rigid path uses its existing mass-centroid representation. These densities are
interval averages. da_eff uses the physical normal change projected on the total
